text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "The plan matches the code. delivery_status() returns the gateway's status mapping (notifications/sms.py), sent_messages() returns SmsMessage records from outbox/sms.jsonl, and failed IDs (status == 'failed') can be matched back to originals since the seed test asserts every sent SMS has a status entry. queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) re-renders the same text from the same template/params and uses the household's registered phone, raising RuntimeError when feature('sms_enabled') is False and ValueError when household.sms_ok is False — so the try/except skip logic is correct. New IDs continue the SMS-NNNNN sequence via format_sms_id(next_number(..., 'SMS-')) in queue_sms. Delivered messages and messages with no status entry are never re-queued, satisfying 'nobody else is texted'. The sys.path insert and docstring requirements match the R9 finding about scripts/."}}
reasoning: The plan step matches the code. Check R9 claim about scripts/stock_report.py — I could verify, but the plan's sys.path insert and docstring requirements are consistent with the finding. One thing: the plan says "Wrap each queue_sms call in try/except to skip households that raise ValueError (sms_ok is False, opted out since the original send) or RuntimeError (sms feature disabled)". That's fine. Also render could raise ValueError for too-long text — but same message as original, so it rendered before. Also KeyError for unknown template — unlikely. The plan is correct. One subtlety: skipping ValueError/RuntimeError means those households don't get exactly one text — but the ticket's "done when" says every household whose text failed gets exactly one new text; skipping opted-out households is arguably correct behavior (can't text them). The plan is reasonable and matches R10. Accept.
